historical_record.description: The Presidio branch of the San Francisco Public Library, designed by G. Albert Lansburgh.
Photographed, showing the Presidio Branch Library.
The City Planning Commission approved the designation of the Presidio Branch Carnegie Library as Landmark No. 240 and recommended it to the Board of Supervisors.

In April 1990 the city presented plans to renovate the Presidio Branch Library, then 69 years old: a seismic upgrade, new wiring and better disabled access, with the branch to close for six to eight months.
The Presidio Branch Library closed for renovation on March 24, 1991: a seismic upgrade, disabled access, rewiring and asbestos removal, paid for by a bond measure passed in November 1988.
The Presidio Branch Library was due to reopen in late January 1992 after a renovation that brought a seismic upgrade, asbestos removal, new wiring, a new roof and disabled access.
The Presidio Branch Library opened here in April 1921, in a brick and terra cotta building in the Italian Renaissance style.
By October 2003 the Presidio Branch Library had been nominated for city landmark status. It was built in 1921 with a Carnegie grant, one of seven Carnegie branch libraries in San Francisco.
On July 8, 2008 the library presented plans for an interior renovation of the Presidio Branch Library by the firms Field Paoli and Joseph Chow & Associates.

The Library Commission designated the Presidio Branch Library at 3150 Sacramento Street as the site of a federally funded Communications Center and Media Literacy Project, with a ramp, a ground-level entrance and an elevator for disabled patrons to be added with federal funds.
The Presidio Branch Library reopened on January 28, 1992, with its renovation and seismic strengthening complete.

unknowns: Accounts differ on when the Presidio Branch Library closed for its 1991 renovation: March 24 or May.
